summary: The note describes the rise of green construction, a life-cycle approach to building that uses environmentally responsible, resource-efficient processes and materials. It walks through design, materials, water efficiency, energy, indoor environmental quality, and waste reduction, citing local figures and companies with dated announcements. It closes on certifications, client education and the role of local government in encouraging sustainable building.
one_line: Overview of local green construction trends in 2023, covering eco-friendly materials, water and energy efficiency, waste reduction, certification and policy support.
key_facts: Green construction, also called sustainable building, covers a building's whole life cycle: design, construction, operation, maintenance, renovation, and demolition.
Local architect Melissa Turner hosted a roundtable on October 5, 2023, saying "Green construction begins with design; it's more than just adding solar panels on a roof."
Building orientation can reduce energy use by taking advantage of the sun's path to maximize natural heating and lighting.
On September 30, 2023, Innovate Materials Corp CEO Dr. Samuel Peterson announced a new bio-brick made from recycled materials and locally sourced agricultural waste.
Dr. Samuel Peterson said the bio-bricks have a smaller carbon footprint and maintain the same if not better insulation than traditional materials.
Recycled steel is a high-strength material that allows less material to be used without compromising safety or aesthetic appeal.
Jasmine Liu led a water conservation workshop on November 6, 2023, noting modern developments recycle greywater for toilet flushing and landscape watering.
The Solar Tiles Company launched a solar roofing product on September 15, 2023; CEO Angela Richardson claims it could produce as much as 70% of a household's energy needs.
Innovate Living announced an "IEQ-first" project on October 22, 2023; project manager Alberto Gomez cited biophilic design, natural light, and non-toxic materials.
Construction manager Evan Roberts reported on November 21, 2023 that his site cut waste going to landfill by 30% through planning and strict recycling protocols.
Certifications such as LEED, BREEAM, or local green building standards provide frameworks and incentives for green construction.
Councilwoman Sara Nguyen advocates tax credits for homeowners choosing green solutions and stricter building codes favoring energy efficiency.
